subject: ACME - Private observability: evidence path & SIEM ingest provisioning
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Benson <lara.benson@acme-corp.com>, Mark Hughes <mark.hughes@acme-corp.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME - Private observability: evidence path & SIEM ingest provisioning

Hi Lara / Mark —

Thanks for taking the call last week. Per our conversation, attaching a first-pass runbook for how Redwood will surface logs/traces/metrics out of the private deployment for SIEM ingestion and audit evidence. The high-level options we discussed are in the doc; I called out the recommended path (forwarder inside customer VPC -> local Splunk HEC endpoint or S3 staging with presigned URLs) so we can meet your egress policy.

Before we lock the runbook, can you confirm the following from your side?
- Allowed egress: can the forwarder open outbound TLS (443) to a Splunk HEC endpoint inside your VPC, or do we need to strictly use S3 staging?
- Token/credential rotation: do you require short-lived tokens (rotated daily) or can we use long-lived HEC tokens behind internal KMS?
- Retention/audit bundle expectations: which artifacts do you want included in the evidence bundle for SOC/audit (sample logs, redacted traces, request/response headers)?
- Trace correlation: confirm the header/key you want us to emit (x-acme-trace-id or a different field) so your tracing system correlates Redwood-generated spans with application traces.

I attached: acme-obsv-runbook-draft.pdf (see section 3 for options matrix).

If you can reply with the items above we’ll update the runbook and propose a short runbook review (30 minutes) with the eng/ops team.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachment: acme-obsv-runbook-draft.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

> Hi Kimberly —
>
> Really appreciate the doc. A few quick points from security/ops:
>
> 1) Splunk HEC inside our VPC is preferred; we do not want general outbound to public SaaS endpoints from our sensitive subnets.
> 2) HEC tokens must be rotated; prefer short-lived tokens (24h) that we can issue via our internal vault. Can Redwood support dynamic token fetch from a Vault endpoint at startup and token refresh for long-running forwarders?
> 3) For evidence bundles we need: original request logs (headers redacted except trace id), a sample of generated output for 100 requests, server-side audit log (user, timestamp, route/model), and a signed manifest.
> 4) We require mTLS for any ingestion endpoint in the VPC; TLS-only is insufficient for production.
>
> Can we get a simple implementation stub showing how Redwood would do token fetch + mTLS for HEC? Also want to understand what metadata you will include in logs to tie to our internal session ids.
>
> Thanks,
> Lara
> Director, Security Engineering
> Acme Corp

> Subject: Re: ACME - Private observability: evidence path & SIEM ingest provisioning
>
> Kim / Jordan —
>
> Quick technical notes from runtime/serving team:
>
> 1) Token fetch & rotation: yes, the forwarder in-customer VPC can be configured to request short-lived HEC tokens from ACME's vault during startup and refresh them before expiry. We currently support a Vault plugin that requests a token via an auth role; the forwarder stores tokens in-memory and rotates them on a configurable interval. We'll add an option to re-request a token on 401 from the HEC.
>
> 2) mTLS: the runtime supports client certificate presentation. We recommend the customer host a Splunk HEC behind an Application Load Balancer that accepts client certs; the forwarder will mount a client cert (coming from a secret mount or KMS-translated cert) and present it on TLS handshake. We'll provide a client cert hot-reload path for cert rotations.
>
> 3) Evidence bundle: we'll assemble an evidence archive per export cycle. Contents: request log (redacted headers apart from trace id), response snapshot (first 100 outputs sampling by route/model), runtime audit logs (start/stop, config hash, user id), and a signed manifest (signed with the customer-integrated HSM/KMS key or Redwood signing key depending on contract). Format: gzipped tar with manifest.json.
>
> 4) Alternate when egress is prohibited: S3 staging with presigned PUT URLs (customer-hosted S3 inside their account) is supported. Forwarder stages bundles to S3 with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and the customer can pull bundles on their schedule. This reduces the need for long-lived open connections.
>
> I attached a quick sample config for Splunk HEC + Vault flow (splunk-hec-sample-config.txt).
>
> Next steps: we can prepare a minimal runbook that maps to ACME's Vault and ALB setup and include the cert rotation steps.
>
> Tessa
> Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
> Attachment: splunk-hec-sample-config.txt (TXT, 6KB)

>
> - For audits we need the trace correlation key to be present in both raw request logs and in the manifest (please use header name x-acme-trace-id).
> - Evidence retention: we will pull bundles weekly for the first 90 days; ensure bundles are available in S3 staging for at least 14 days if you buffer them.
> - Audit trail: include the forwarder config hash and the runtime version in the manifest; this is important for our compliance team.
>
> Can you send a one-page stub we can hand to our platform team (network/security) showing the required ALB listener config (ports/ciphers) and the token fetch URL pattern? That will speed procurement.

Lara / Mark —

Thanks for the clarifications, great to have alignment. Summary and agreed actions below:

Agreed approach:
- Splunk HEC inside ACME VPC behind ALB with mTLS. Forwarder will present client certs and rotate via hot-reload.
- Short-lived HEC tokens (24h) delivered by ACME Vault; forwarder will fetch at startup and rotate on schedule / on 401s.
- Evidence bundles staged to ACME S3 (presigned PUT from forwarder) and retained for 14 days; ACME will pull weekly for 90-day retention.
- Manifest will include: trace header (x-acme-trace-id), forwarder config hash, runtime version, timestamp, and signed manifest signature.

Action items / owners:
- Redwood (Tessa): produce ALB listener stub (ports, required ciphers, cert handling) + small sample config for token fetch URL and Vault role by 2026-10-25. (Attachment: splunk-hec-rotation-guide.txt)
- Redwood (Jordan): update runbook on Drive to include the S3 staging flow and evidence manifest schema by 2026-10-27. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/acme/onboarding/runbook-v1
- ACME (Lara): confirm Vault role name and whether the forwarder should call vault.example.internal/v1/issue/hec as the token endpoint.
- ACME (Mark / ops): confirm ALB listener cert requirements and if your infra team will accept our client certs or provision certs into a shared KMS/HSM.

I'll schedule a 30-minute runbook review for 2026-10-26; invite should hit your calendars today.

If anyone needs the one-page stub sooner, ping me and I’ll surface it.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
